summary: Susquehanna County steel fire tower of 1921, 60 feet tall, removed before 1989; a 2008 survey visit found concrete supports and a step still in place.

facts.status_note: Removed before 1989 per the register; in 2008 several concrete supports and a concrete step remained.

events.note: Erected by the Pennsylvania Department of Forestry; November 1921 newspaper item and register both give 1921
Survey mark recovery on October 12, 2008 recorded concrete supports and the concrete step still in place

evidence.supports: Pennsylvania Department of Forestry erected a steel fire tower on Elk Hill in Susquehanna County
evidence.quote: The Pennsylvania Department of Forestry has erected a steel fire tower, 60 feet in height, in Susquehanna county, on Elk Hill.

evidence.supports: tower gave a view for prompt detection of woodland fires
evidence.quote: From here an extensive view is afforded permitting the prompt detection of fires in the woods.

evidence.supports: tower did not protect the entire county
evidence.quote: Of course this does not protect the entire county

evidence.supports: item attributed to The Montrose Democrat
steel Aermotor tower built 1921 and removed before 1989
evidence.quote: This steel Aermotor tower was built in 1921 and was removed before 1989.

evidence.supports: several concrete supports and the concrete step remain
evidence.quote: Several of the concrete supports remain, as does the concrete step into which TT 24 A is set.

evidence.supports: concrete slab was the base for the steps climbing the tower
evidence.quote: a concrete slab that served as the base for the steps climbing the lookout tower

evidence.supports: benchmark TT 24 A set in the concrete slab at the tower site
evidence.quote: USGS bench mark disk TT 24 A, which is set into a concrete slab that served as the base for the steps climbing the lookout tower

evidence.supports: mark recovered in destroyed condition on October 12, 2008
evidence.quote: Recovered in Destroyed Condition on October 12, 2008

evidence.supports: setting listed as a fire lookout tower

notes_for_editor: No exact removal year found; 'before 1989' is the register's bound, so no removal event is recorded. The only description of what remains is one survey-mark page from a single 2008 visit. Wikipedia gives the summit as 2,693 ft (821 m) while the register gives the site as 2,678 ft (816 m); these are probably summit versus site figures, not a conflict about the tower, and the record keeps 816 m. The survey page's 1959 date is in the mark's name only and is not used. Visitor access was not established.
